CATALYTIC COMPLETION AS AN ASSEMBLY EXIT: PROOFS AND FAILURES
2026-11-01. Original construction and analysis in this investigation.
Status: mathematical and molecular construction; no new wet-lab result.

Purpose: recover a working physical RNA-protein machine while retaining the
chemistry of the RNA that was manufactured. Recovering its DNA sequence is a
different operation. Reverse transcription/transcription do not reproduce a
complete modification pattern or assembled state.

No variable below is assigned a favorable experimental value for the new
realization. Rates from short peptides, isolated domains, other organisms or
other immobilization geometries are not substituted.

1. LOAD PATH: WHY COLLECTION IS NOT AN EXACT CATALYTIC CERTIFICATE

A ribosome is halted at a stop codon without class-I release factors. Capture
its nascent product through a distal affinity handle outside the exit tunnel.
The connection is support--handle--peptide--ester--tRNA--ribosome, with further
noncovalent peptide/tunnel contacts. The intended event is cognate-RF-promoted
ester hydrolysis, followed by physical exit of the same manufactured subunits.

Proposition 1. Collection certifies a chosen catalytic event exactly only if
every accessible path to collection crosses that event, and the collected
object is the candidate that traversed the path.

Proof. A noncertifying path with nonzero probability is a counterexample.
A passenger is also a counterexample. Conversely the two conditions force
the identified collected object's trajectory through the event.

This physical design DOES NOT satisfy an exact cut condition. Peptidyl-tRNA
can dissociate intact; the affinity attachment can dissociate; hydrolysis can
occur without correct stop recognition. Multiple ribosomes can share a
message. completion_exit.py explicitly enumerates these bypasses.

The original simultaneous termination/recycling version adds an avoidable
bypass: RF3/RRF/EF-G can promote peptidyl-tRNA drop-off. It is rejected.
The corrected version collects a class-I-RF-only eluate FIRST and recycles it
in a separate vessel. Sufficient RF1 for a single-turnover pulse is charged;
efficient RF1 cycling on the support is not assumed. This removes one
reagent-enabled bypass, not intrinsic leakage.

Therefore the operation offers at most calibrated probabilistic enrichment.

CHEMICAL ASSEMBLY AND COMPLETION-DEPENDENT RECOVERY
Research record, 2026-11-01

STATUS
This is a source-constrained molecular construction and an experimental
decision, not a new wet-lab result. No assembly yield, kinetic discrimination,
fidelity or lifetime is inferred from a contact graph or assigned to the new
construct. Existing catalytic selection, ribosome display, covalent RNA
ligation and natural remodeling are credited as existing machinery.

THE SERVICE
Manufacture a continuous, chemically specified 23S RNA without extracting
that RNA from a preexisting ribosome; assemble it with explicit structural
proteins; recover the same manufactured 50S/23S lineage after a complete
translation challenge; and obtain repeated, accurate protein output over a
declared working interval. Small subunits, tRNAs, translation factors, energy
regeneration and processing enzymes remain explicit supplied components.

The long-term consequence would be a chemically programmable route to
large RNA-protein machines, with the ribosome as an unusually consequential
first target. It would remove a native-RNA/extract dependence in the productive
path. It would not by itself produce a self-replicating factory, manufacture
modified monomers, or eliminate biological production of supplied enzymes.

The independent chemical construction is now the main manufacturing lead.
The root completion-exit construction is a candidate qualification/harvesting
operation within it. The informed conventional competitor already provides
most of the same recovery service. I do not make uniqueness or total-cost
advantage claims for the proposed RF exit.

1. MAKE THE RNA BEFORE ASKING A PROTEIN-CONTAINING INTERMEDIATE TO RELEASE A GUIDE

The exact reference, modification map, patches, spacers, seams and splints
are in stage2_alternative/data. Native 3'-5' continuity is retained. Nine
modified patches plus ten IVT spacers cover all2904nt. Nine ternary ligation
operations seal18seams. Splints are removed BEFORE protein assembly. RlmKL
and SAM supply two methylations that are not assumed chemically accessible
in the same way as the other23 marks. The specified pattern is a25-site
target, not a claim of identical occupancy in every native preparation.

RESET, RECOVERABLE FUNCTION, AND THE STRONG CONVENTIONAL COMPETITOR
Independent construction by assembly_existing, 2026-11-01.
Scope: conclusions from primary evidence and conditional mathematics; no new wet-lab result.

DECISION

An experimentally real structural reset exists. It does not yet establish that resetting
the actual failed manufacture fraction creates additional active ribosomes. Moreover,
selective export before resetting is not unique to RF-dependent on-bead release:
competitive affinity recovery can protect the same successful RNA-containing objects.
Global factors-only maturation is the strongest first comparator. If it preserves active
material while providing the same repair, selection has no yield rationale.

EXACT CURRENT RESET EVIDENCE

Sato et al., eLife 15:RP109916, version of record 2026-06-18.
DOI: 10.7554/eLife.109916.4
https://elifesciences.org/articles/109916
Local full text: ../stage2_alternative/sources/elife109916.txt and .xml.

Native ribosomes were exposed to EDTA on ice for 30 min. Written inputs: 0.5 uL
of 5 uM ribosome plus 1 uL of 100 mM EDTA; pretreatment EDTA approximately 67 mM.
All 1.5 uL entered a 10-uL PURE reaction: 0.5 uL PUREfrex 2.0 enzyme mix,
0.2 ug each EngA/ObgE, 150 mM potassium glutamate, 32 mM total magnesium acetate,
5 nM sfGFP DNA, 37 C. The volume/concentration imply 2.5 pmol ribosome, whereas
Methods twice states 0.5 pmol. Final EDTA implied by volumes is 10 mM. Free Mg
was not independently quantified.

Figure 8 shows fluorescence over 480 min, with recovery only with both factors.
It supplies no untreated-native calibration, absolute particle recovery, repeated
cycles, or post-reset modification map. The separate approximately 60% estimate
is a fluorescence-rate calibration of de novo assembly, not EDTA recovery.
Native-derived TP70 contains additional biogenesis factors; transcript assembly
with the two factors failed. Therefore transfer to chemically constructed RNA
and all-recombinant failed particles remains untested.

The argument below is our inference and competing construction, rather than a
reported experiment.
